name: Euro-area economy
value: Q3 GDP +0.4% (13 Nov est.); Oct PMI 51.9
summary: Eurostat's 13 Nov estimate keeps euro-area Q3 GDP growth at 0.4% with employment stable; October flash PMI 51.9
state: Eurostat's estimate published on 13 Nov kept euro-area GDP growth at 0.4% in the third quarter, with employment stable, confirming the 30 Oct flash (Eurostat). The October flash composite PMI of 51.9 remains above 50. Both readings sit above the Normal lines.
for_you: Steady growth supports jobs and incomes across the euro area. Rising interest rates in Europe and the US tend to slow activity over the following quarters, with heavily indebted firms and households most exposed.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% (positive) and October composite PMI 51.9 > 50

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% and employment stable in the euro area

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
